construct: Tissue transglutaminase deamidates selected glutamine residues in gluten peptides to glutamate, increasing their negative charge and affinity for disease-associated HLA-DQ2/DQ8 molecules. Presentation of these peptides to CD4+ T cells drives mucosal inflammation and villous injury.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Celiac disease is driven by tissue-transglutaminase deamidation of gluten peptides, increasing their negative charge and affinity for HLA-DQ2/DQ8 and enhancing CD4 T-cell presentation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: IgE cross-linking, complement-mediated enterocyte lysis, MHC-independent superantigen activation, and HLA-DQ suppression are incompatible with the established tTG–deamidated gluten–HLA-DQ2/DQ8 pathway.
